This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Chili was surrendered to the care center as a stray and we have no history on his behavior in a home environment. Chili showed fearful and defensive behavior on first entering the care center, hard barking at staff and showing tense body language during handling. Over time he has shown increasing comfort in his interactions with handlers, but has shown escalating arousal, including jumping up and mouthing on walks, and pulling towards and barking at other dogs. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner, who can allow for decompression, provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Chili is one handsome boy with a heart of gold! He may be a little nervous when first meeting new people, but give him a little time and patience to settle in, and his sweet personality begins to shine. He's just looking for someone who will let him come out of his shell at his own pace.
After our walk, Chili gave me the sweetest little kisses, almost as if he was thanking me for taking him out, and then rested his head right on my lap for some snuggles. It was such a precious moment and a glimpse of just how loving this boy can be once he feels comfortable. â¤ï¸
Chili is looking for a patient, loving home where he can feel safe, build confidence, and show off all the sweetness he has to offer. I promise he's worth taking the time to get to know! ðŸ¥¹

A volunteer writes: Chili was found in one of my favorite places in the whole city. But, I'm sure his memories and recollections about that NYC park are quite different from mine. Chili was rescued by park rangers after being discovered tied to the stairs. And though that was over three months ago, it doesn't seem the trauma of that day has fully dissipated for him. Chili has been doing his best to be a good resident: sitting for treats, playing fetch, keeping his kennel clean...but we still see a fairly anxious/fearful pup on walks and when faced with new situations. Still, he maintains a sweet and earnest demeanor that we just love and we have no doubt in a less chaotic environment, his personality will really shine through. Chili will do well with an experienced family with kids 13+ that will let him acclimate at his own pace. They should move slowly with him and help to build positive associations and let him be the one to initiate interactions with people.
